result:
**Verdict: PASS**, with one new Low, non-mandatory finding (F-DG0-171). I reviewed frozen candidate `sha256:1af91e8f620aec37…` at source commit `331407e`, and the recomputed candidate ID matches. HEAD is one commit later (`57d7a53`); that commit changes only metadata, no candidate path. The clone is complete, not shallow.

**The D-044 change (F-DG0-250) works.** I made real annotated-tag objects in disposable `--no-local` clones and ran each forgery against both the pre-D-044 baseline (`49b5ad7`) and the candidate:

| Forgery | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `fix_revision` set to a tag that points at the real fix commit | accepted | rejected ("is a tag object, not a commit") |
| `fix_revision` set to a tag of a tag | accepted | rejected |
| `head_commit_at_start` set to a tag, on the run that verified the closure | accepted | rejected (2 errors) |
| `head_commit_at_start` set to a tag, on a run that verified no closure | accepted | rejected |
| Gate `source_commit` set to a tag (the older D-037 rule) | – | still rejected |
| `fix_revision` set to a tree id, a blob id or uppercase hex | – | rejected |
| Lightweight tag (resolves to the commit itself) | – | passes, no false positive |

On the candidate, the only errors these forgeries produce are the object-type errors, so the new check is what rejects them.

**The standing controls still hold.** My round-24 to round-27 reproductions give the same results as last round. The one expected failure, SEC24-2, has failed by design since D-042 and is replaced by SEC26-2.

**The real repository is clean:**
- All 118 `fix_revision` values are commit objects.
- Every `head_commit_at_start` that exists is a commit object. The 3 that are missing all belong to round 18's orphaned commit, a case already covered by D-034/D-035.
- The 117 verified closures show no failures on any of the three commit anchors.
- The gate dry run shows 0 in every history category and no object-type errors.

**Other checks all passed:**
- **Tests:** node 103/103, Python 22/22 and the pre-freeze check 11/11.
- **Candidate ID:** the same across working tree, `--ref`, directory, locale, time zone and umask.
- **Validator:** exit codes are correct in every mode.
- **Malformed input:** bad CSV or JSON fails closed.
- **CI:** read-only token, actions pinned to full SHAs, full history checked out. No secrets found, and settings auto-allow only `Bash(bwrap:*)`.
- **Sandbox:** every protected or other-role write was refused. Residual 7 (host-wide `/proc/sys` writable, F-DG0-149) and residual 8 (process visibility only) are exactly as the threat model describes.
- **Requirements:** all 19 DG0-final requirements are IMPLEMENTED, their evidence files exist, and their cited tests passed in my own runs.

**New finding: F-DG0-171 (Low, not a mandatory violation, owner delivery-orchestrator)**
- **The gap:** a review round's `source_commit` (in `stages.json` and the round manifest) still accepts an annotated-tag id. `findManifest` (`rules.mjs:918`), `checkReviewRounds` (`rules.mjs:774-775`) and closure anchor 1 (`rules.mjs:750-752`) all resolve the tag to its commit and don't check the type. My probe SEC28-8 shows `findManifest` returns 0 errors for a tag there. This contradicts D-044's claim that it covers "every commit-id field the gate depends on".
- **Why it isn't a bypass:**
  - The freeze tool always writes a commit id.
  - The gate's own round must match the gate `source_commit`, which is type-checked.
  - A tag only points at the same commit, so the checks still judge the right commit.
  - If the tag is deleted, a fresh clone lacks it, and any closure verified in that round is rejected.
- **Suggested fix:** check the object type in `checkReviewRounds` whenever the object is present, and correct D-044's wording.
- **My position:** I recorded my agreement to accept it as an observation. It only takes effect if the release-auditor also agrees; the orchestrator can fix it instead.

I did not re-verify F-DG0-250, because it is qa's finding.

**Three things you should know:**
- **Probe side effect:** one of my ad-hoc probe commands accidentally created an empty top-level `package.json` on the sandbox's throwaway layer. That briefly changed the working-tree candidate ID. I deleted it, recomputed the ID and recorded the incident in `candidate-and-scope.log`. It never reached git or the real tree.
- **Base-commit slip:** my requirements script first compared `trading_agent/` against the wrong base commit. The correct base, `f099f3d`, shows it unchanged; the correction is in `requirements-check.log`.
- **Round number:** `review-common.md` says "Review round: 23" but names round-28 paths. I followed the paths, which match `stages.json`.

Independence: I authored nothing in the reviewed scope and read no other round-28 review. The domain and qa records appeared in git during my run; I didn't open them. The disposable clones are removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-28/`:
- code-security-reviewer.json
- code-security-reviewer.findings.json
- code-security-reviewer.verifications.json
- code-security-reviewer.md

Evidence (19 files) is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-28/`.
